advisory committees as well as council and administration about discretionary spending by advisory committees,
especially as it relates to consistency across committees, overlap with existing city programs or grants,
and how committee requests fit within broader budget decisions made by city council. Based on that,
last month council made a motion asking the administration to look at this more closely. And in March,
we brought forward a number of options for council's consideration for revised approaches.
What council has ultimately decided to do is to, for committees to retain the authority to approve
discretionary spending of up to $2,000, when it is clearly within the mandate of the committee and within
the approved budget that council has provided to the committee. Any request that exceed that or overlap
with existing programs or budget decisions would go forward from the advisory committee in the
form of a recommendation to the appropriate standing policy committee. Recognizing that this can have
an impact on kind of the back end administration of some of the advisory committees. We are also providing
a standardization of how requests are reviewed administratively. So before a funding request is received
at the table by an advisory committee, what we are proposing to do is to have administration provide
background information that would include whether or not there's a grant program that the city
already has that could apply to the fund. Whether this work is already delivered by administration
and whether or not a similar request may have been considered through council's budget process,
whether that was approved or denied. That information would come to the advisory committee in advance.
And if needed, would go forward to the SPC along with any recommendation that may be made by the advisory
committee. In addition to this, there is a change that in how advisory committee budgets will be presented
and approved by city council. Right now advisory committees have a kind of a rolling status
school budget that comes forward as part of the overall city clerk's office budget, but it's not broken
out specifically in the documents that city council approves. What is going to change is we will be
asking each advisory committee to actually create and submit an individual budget and we will
provide administrative assistance to do so and we would ask that the advisory committee approved this
by October 1st each year and then that information would come forward as an actual agenda item for council
to approve during budget. So council would be approving each of the advisory committees individual budgets.
The intent of this is not at all to limit the really great work or the discussion that occurs at
advisory committees. It's just to make sure that we are streamlining our processes as much as possible
and we are eliminating instances where there is confusion, especially where there are more than one fund
that is being used to fund different kinds of work around the city. As an example, there may be programs
that an advisory committee is providing funds towards or an event. And at the same time, there's already
money that council has approved through an administrative budget to go towards that. So it doesn't make
